would like to share something with you ladies and gents too. Yes men can get breast cancer so check yourselves guys.

I bothered to hold on for a long while and got a nurse appointment.

I presented with a lump and thought I had breast cancer, the charming nurse I saw was wonderful!, she did a referral for me telling me, quite clearly,
I would be going under suspected cancer referral and try not to worry as it was probably not, but best to check.

When I got to hosp, within a week, had mammogram, ultrasound and visit with x 2 consultants to be told outcome all within 2 hours!!!

Amazing NHS absolutely wonderful, so just a little note of joy from me all clear and could not believe how kind and efficient everybody was from receptionist upwards.

There are some good guys at Cowes who want to help, not all, granted but that's down to training and as an ex medical secretary they do need some help in some departments.

All in all hold on, try to be clear and concise about what you want, maybe write a tick list so when you get through you are ready to tell them your problem.

They are inundated in mornings so being prepared helps you and them,  try to stay calm and focused and most of all be a patient patient!, it may help you long term to do so. My husband and I  been treated with respect and friendliness.
Although they have too many patients, they do their best to see everyone as soon as possible and try to give each patient the time and attention they need.

The GPs that I have seen have been friendly, actively listening, knowledgeable and quick to test and treat.

All other staff, including reception staff and on the phone, have always been respectful, helpful, friendly and professional.
